title: Ashton Jeanty, revamped O-line power Raiders’ win over Dolphins in Klint Kubiak’s debut
content:
LAS VEGAS — Ashton Jeanty and the Las Vegas Raiders opened their season by taking down the Miami Dolphins 27-13 on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Jeanty looked like the superstar running back Raiders fans hoped he would be with an improved offensive line and ecosystem around him. The No. 6 pick in last year’s draft piled up 147 total yards and two receiving touchdowns to lead Las Vegas to a win in coach Klint Kubiak’s coaching debut.

Box score | Week 1 live blog | Game discussion

That he’s seemed to vastly improve the Raiders’ offensive trench play and running game.

Las Vegas fielded the NFL’s worst offensive line a season ago, allowing a league-high 64 sacks, which stifled its passing attack. But on Sunday, veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins had a ton of time to work, allowing him to operate decisively and efficiently. Cousins, making his regular-season Raiders debut, was clinical in the first half, going 14-for-17 passing for 96 yards and two touchdowns, including the 300th of his career. While he was quick to get the ball out of his hands, he operated out of clean pockets, giving him clean opportunities. Cousins added a third passing touchdown in the second and finished 21-of-30 passing for 160 yards and three scores. That last touchdown gave Cousins 301 for his career, surpassing John Elway for 14th all time.

Cousins looked a little shaky throwing downfield, tossing a pick to Dolphins rookie Michael Taaffe to start the third quarter and another to Dante Trader Jr. in the fourth. But that wasn’t his protection’s fault; it gave him time to take the deep shots he wanted to.

Las Vegas also dominated on the ground, allowing Jeanty’s second season to get off to a strong start. The running back had all kinds of room to run as new center Tyler Linderbaum led the push from the interior. Jeanty was consistently contacted in the backfield as a rookie, but with free space ahead of him Sunday, he looked every bit like a top-10 pick. It wasn’t just Jeanty, either; rookie running back Mike Washington (seven carries, 41 yards) found space, too, allowing him to showcase the explosiveness we saw in the preseason.

If Kubiak has indeed forged the Raiders’ front into a consistently competent unit, he can make the Raiders a consistently competitive team. Their performance in Week 1 is a sign the coach can help bring success back to this franchise.

Absolutely. Jeanty’s performance was reminiscent of his college days at Boise State, when he looked unstoppable. With room to run, he had a chance to go on the offensive, and rarely did the first Dolphins defender bring him down. Even when he was tackled, he was pushing the ball forward, such as when he went flying for a few extra yards on a big third-down run in the third quarter. He finished with 102 yards on 23 carries.

But perhaps even more exciting was what he did in the passing game, recording six receptions for 45 yards and two touchdowns. He had some run as a receiver in his rookie year, catching 55 passes for 346 yards and five touchdowns. Most of those were just ways to get him out from behind the offensive line, however. His connections with Cousins on Sunday made him look like a legitimate dual threat from the backfield, running routes down the field and getting open against linebackers and defensive backs. It will strain opposing defenses if he can continue to do that effectively.

There were many questions about who would be the focal point of the Raiders’ offense with Brock Bowers out. Jeanty stepped up Sunday; it looks like he can be a go-to guy moving forward.

Crosby, who had 1.5 sacks, made public what he showed in training camp: He looks like he is back to being a game-wrecker.

The five-time Pro Bowler grew tired of questions this offseason about his surgically repaired knee — the one that led to a failed physical with the Ravens, nixing a trade to Baltimore. He has repeatedly said he was fine and happy to be back with the Raiders. His performance Sunday proved that.

Crosby drew a lot of attention from the Dolphins’ offensive line, opening early opportunities for teammates such as Kwity Paye (two sacks) and Folorunso Fatukasi (0.5 sacks) to get into the backfield. Then, with the Raiders up two touchdowns in the fourth quarter, he finally got his chance to hunt with the Dolphins forced to pass.

He beat Miami left tackle Patrick Paul inside as quarterback Malik Willis scrambled on a third down, picking up his first sack and breaking the career 70-sack mark, making him the third Raiders player to do so. On the next third down, he beat right tackle Austin Jackson, converging on Willis with Paye for another half-sack.

Crosby wasn’t out there on every down like we’ve seen him in the past. He was off the field for the majority of the Dolphins’ third drive before coming in to finish it. He stayed on the sidelines for some early downs before helping close out the Dolphins with his rush.

When asked about Crosby sitting out those few plays, Kubiak simply said, “That’s my call.”

It’s possible the Raiders had him on a pitch count. That would be reasonable, even if he were completely back to full strength. Either way, the added rest seemed to help.

Willis has promise if the Dolphins provide him some help.

Willis was under duress from the Raiders’ pass rush for most of the day, getting sacked five times while tossing one interception. But the pressure put his athleticism on display, such as when he scrambled in for a touchdown in the third quarter. Willis also showed off his arm talent with big passes downfield to receivers Malik Washington, Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas. He finished 15-for-27 passing for 220 yards and added 39 yards on the ground.

Willis definitely needed to do a better job operating the offense. And he made some aggressive mistakes, such as when he completely missed seeing Treydan Stukes over the middle, giving the Raiders’ rookie safety his first career interception. Some of that was because he was playing aggressively with the Dolphins behind for much of the game.

Outside of running back De’Von Achane (11 carries, 36 yards), whom the Raiders clearly had a plan for, the Dolphins didn’t provide Willis with a ton of support. Miami is clearly in a rebuilding year. The Dolphins are trying to get a lot of dead money off their books, which is forcing them to play a lot of replacement-level players. It’s early, but Willis could show he is worthy of sticking around after things clear up.
